proofs.full_local_argument: Define U_{n-1}(cos theta)=sin(n theta)/sin theta and w(t)=(t^2-1)U_{n-1}(t). Its n+1 simple roots are exactly t_j. Since n-1 is even, w is even and w'(0)=0; U_{n-1}(0)=s_n, hence w(0)=-s_n. For an interior node theta_j=j*pi/n, differentiate U(cos theta): U'(t_j)=-n*(-1)^j/sin(theta_j)^2. Multiplying by t_j^2-1=-sin(theta_j)^2 gives w'(t_j)=n*(-1)^j. At 1, w'(1)=2U(1)=2n; at -1, U(-1)=n and w'(-1)=-2n. Thus uniformly w'(t_j)=n*c_j*(-1)^j, including n=1. The Lagrange cardinal polynomial l_j(t)=w(t)/((t-t_j)w'(t_j)) has l_j'(0)=-w(0)/(t_j^2*w'(t_j))=s_n*(-1)^j/(n*c_j*t_j^2)=h*d_j. Interpolation gives P(h*t)=sum_j P(h*t_j)l_j(t); differentiate at zero and divide by h to obtain the first identity. Taking P constant yields sum_j d_j=0. Finally T_n(cos theta)=cos(n theta) implies T_n(t_j)=(-1)^j and T_n'(0)=n*sin(n*pi/2)=n*s_n. Apply the first identity to P(t)=T_n(t/h): sum_j d_j*(-1)^j=n*s_n/h. Every d_j*(-1)^j has sign s_n, so the left side equals s_n*sum_j|d_j|. Division by s_n proves W=n/h. Vector-valued interpolation holds componentwise.

assumptions: h>0; P is any vector-valued polynomial of degree at most n over a real finite-dimensional vector space.
All n+1 nodes, including both endpoints with their factor c_j=2, are retained. Odd n ensures t_j is never zero.
statement.conclusion: sum_{j=0}^n d_j P(h*t_j)=P'(0); sum_{j=0}^n d_j=0; W:=sum_{j=0}^n |d_j|=n/h.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let n>=1 be odd, t_j=cos(j*pi/n), j=0,...,n, c_0=c_n=2 and c_j=1 otherwise. Set s_n=(-1)^((n-1)/2) and d_j=s_n*(-1)^j/(n*h*c_j*t_j^2).
statement.parameter_domains: Odd integer n>=1; real h>0; arbitrary finite output dimension.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such odd n, radius h and polynomial P, the identities hold deterministically; no stochastic or algorithm-class guarantee is involved.
